title: Single Number Among Triples
statement: A telemetry relay retransmits every sensor reading exactly three times for redundancy, but one reading slipped through the relay exactly once. You are given the non-empty list of received integer readings (values may be negative or zero, and the order is arbitrary): every value appears exactly three times except one value that appears exactly once. Return that lone value as an integer. All values fit in a signed 32-bit integer. Your solution must run in O(n) time using O(1) extra space, so a hash map, set, or sorting is off the table. Note that the pairwise XOR trick does not work here: three copies of a value do not cancel under XOR. Instead, count how often each of the 32 bit positions is set across all readings modulo 3 and reassemble the answer, taking care to interpret bit 31 as the two's-complement sign bit (or use the equivalent ones/twos accumulator technique).
hints: XOR cancels pairs, but here duplicates come in threes. What per-bit statistic would three copies of the same value contribute nothing to?
For each of the 32 bit positions, count how many readings have that bit set. Triples contribute multiples of 3, so count % 3 gives exactly the lone reading's bit at that position.

Loop i from 0 to 31, sum (r >> i) & 1 over all readings, and set bit i of the result when the sum % 3 is nonzero. Since Python ints are unbounded, finish with a sign fix: if result >= 2**31, subtract 2**32 so a set bit 31 becomes a negative number instead of a huge positive one.
